assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks reaching 10^-18 fractional uncertainty are a clean, instrument-driven discovery or invention: the magic-wavelength lattice idea removes Doppler and recoil shifts while retaining many atoms, and the resulting precision opens tests of fundamental constants, relativistic geodesy and a path to redefining the second. The impact is concrete and measurable, which suits a prize for a specific discovery or invention rather than lifetime achievement.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength optical lattice concept and demonstrated early strontium lattice clocks; Ye's group drove the strontium systems to the 10^-18 regime and many-body clock physics. The two supplied names give a coherent pair, though the broader community (other lattice-clock groups, comb developers already honoured in 2005) means credit is not wholly unambiguous.
assessment.maturity: Independent confirmation across several laboratories and species, with international comparisons and a formal roadmap toward redefinition of the second. The interpretation is stable and recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Whether the committee would view the prize as an extension of the 2005 frequency-comb recognition.
My recollection of the precise record uncertainties and which group first crossed 10^-18 is from memory and not verified here.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene opened a platform in which flat moire bands produce correlated insulators and superconductivity that can be tuned electrostatically. The theoretical prediction of flat bands at a magic angle combined with a decisive experiment is a clear discovery with a very wide downstream impact on 2D materials and quantum matter.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald supplied the continuum-model prediction; Jarillo-Herrero's group delivered the 2018 experiments. The decisive experimental first author is not among the credited names, so the three-name configuration is defensible but leaves an allocation question.
assessment.maturity: Replicated by many groups worldwide since 2018 and extended to numerous moire systems. The field is still evolving and the origin of the superconducting pairing remains debated, so interpretation of some phases is not yet settled, though the central discovery is secure.
uncertainties: Unresolved mechanism of superconductivity and some correlated phases.
Credit for early theoretical precursors on twisted-layer electronic structure and for the experimental team members is not fully captured by the supplied names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Room-temperature tunnel magnetoresistance in magnetic tunnel junctions, then very large TMR with MgO barriers, is a discovery and a materials-engineering achievement that underlies read heads and non-volatile magnetic memory. It is a case in which interface structure and crystalline barrier quality decide the physics, a theme I regard as central.
assessment.attribution: Miyazaki and Moodera independently reported room-temperature TMR in 1995; Parkin and, in parallel, Yuasa and colleagues demonstrated the coherent-tunnelling MgO giant TMR in 2004. The supplied names omit the Yuasa/Djayaprawira group, and the theoretical coherent-tunnelling predictions (Butler, Mathon) are also not credited, so attribution is only partly resolved.
assessment.maturity: Over two decades of confirmation and large-scale commercial deployment; the physics is well understood. Recognition could be seen as somewhat overlapping with the 2007 GMR prize, but TMR is a separate discovery.
uncertainties: Split of credit between the 1995 discovery and the 2004 MgO advance, and omission of parallel MgO work.
Overlap with the 2007 prize may weigh against it.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Time-reversal-invariant topological insulators combine a theoretical prediction of a new phase of matter with experimental realisations in HgTe quantum wells and in bismuth-based 3D materials, verified by transport and spectroscopy. The concept is original and has had lasting impact across condensed matter.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele made the foundational Z2 prediction and Molenkamp's group delivered the first experimental observation of the quantum spin Hall state; Hasan led the 3D case with ARPES. A limit of three names forces omission of Mele, and other key theorists and experimentalists (Bernevig, Hughes, Zhang, and others) lie outside the supplied credit, which leaves allocation genuinely contested.
assessment.maturity: Well confirmed by multiple groups and techniques. The topological classification is robust, although practical quantization precision in some systems is limited.
uncertainties: Dropping Eugene J. Mele to fit the three-laureate limit is an unresolved compromise.
Priority disputes around the HgTe proposal and the 3D realisations.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The quantum cascade laser is a genuine invention: it uses engineered intersubband transitions in epitaxial heterostructures to give a laser whose wavelength is set by layer design rather than the bandgap. It created mid-infrared and terahertz semiconductor lasers for spectroscopy and sensing, and depends on atomic-scale control of layers and interfaces, which I find compelling from a structural-characterisation view.
assessment.attribution: The 1994 demonstration at Bell Labs by Faist, Capasso and co-workers, with Cho's molecular beam epitaxy growth, is a clear invention with a compact team. Attribution is relatively clean though other Bell Labs co-authors and earlier intersubband proposals (Kazarinov and Suris) exist.
assessment.maturity: Three decades of development, widely commercial, with strong independent validation. Recognition is timely or even somewhat late.
uncertainties: Role of the earlier Kazarinov-Suris intersubband proposal in priority.
Whether the committee regards a device invention as primarily physics.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical detection and coherent control of single nitrogen-vacancy centres turned a point defect in diamond into a room-temperature spin qubit and nanoscale sensor, with applications in magnetometry, thermometry and biology. It is a very clear discovery-plus-method story with strong links to defect structure in solids.
assessment.attribution: Wrachtrup and Jelezko reported single-NV optical detection and spin readout in 1997 and subsequent coherent control; Lukin's group contributed key quantum-register and sensing demonstrations. Other important contributors (Hanson, Awschalom, Yacoby, Walsworth) are not credited, so the allocation is only partly resolved.
assessment.maturity: Widely replicated and still maturing in sensing. The core discovery is mature; applications are still growing.
uncertainties: Overlap in credit with the related spin-photon interface candidate.
Whether the foundational work or the sensing applications should carry the recognition.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The experimental discovery of the Higgs boson at the LHC, enabled by the conception and construction of the ATLAS and CMS detectors, is among the most important experimental results of the century and completed the Standard Model. The scientific importance is unquestionable.
assessment.attribution: The discovery was a collaborative effort of several thousand people; the three credited names are the originators of the detector projects, but this does not map cleanly onto the discovery itself. The committee has consistently avoided awarding collaborations, and the prize for the theory was given in 2013, so a fair configuration is hard to demonstrate.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed independently by two experiments and subsequent measurements of couplings. Fully mature, though recognition of the experimental side after 2013 is a delicate matter.
uncertainties: Attribution to three individuals for a collaborative discovery is contestable.
Statutes and precedent on recognising instrument builders versus discoverers.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The observation of quantized conductance in ballistic point contacts is a simple and striking discovery of mesoscopic physics that showed conductance quantization in a solid-state device and underpins the later development of quantum nanoelectronics, from quantum dots to Majorana and spin-qubit devices.
assessment.attribution: Two groups reported the effect almost simultaneously in 1988 (Delft/Philips and Cambridge), so a three-person selection must balance both; the Cambridge first author is not among the supplied names, and Pepper's group is represented only through Pepper himself. This leaves an unresolved allocation.
assessment.maturity: Thoroughly confirmed and understood through Landauer-Buttiker theory; it is a mature, settled result, so timing is more than ripe, and arguably recognition has been bypassed by later mesoscopic prizes.
uncertainties: Fair division between the Delft and Cambridge groups and the role of Landauer's theory.
Whether the effect is judged sufficiently distinct from the quantum Hall prize.
